correctness.rationale: Generic suffix maximizers give exactly the composition endpoints; every cut set is realized by giving its ordered endpoints decreasing heights and giving other positions lower heights. Support before n distinguishes cut sets. Adjacent-block merges preserve ||v||^2+2a·v=T^2 because a_s-a_t is the mass of the right block. The simplex projection of -a gives c and the stated consecutive breakpoints, including k=n where the upper condition holds automatically. The nondecreasing c satisfies prefix sums <=jT/n<=prefix supply. Allocating destinations in increasing order therefore gives a feasible supply allocation from sources h<=i and proves c∈Q_n. For vertices, the squared-radius deficit is 2(c+a)·(v-c)>=0. The vertices attaining equality constitute an exposed face containing c; averaging squared distances using their barycentric weights then adds exactly the squared center shift for any competitor, proving uniqueness and minimality. The eligible coordinates are a_i<=lambda, not just a_i<lambda, and give b-1 free cuts. Single-cut differences span the face, which has the known cubical combinatorial type. Successive differences verify the squared-binomial sum, and the breakpoints give k~b~(3/2)^(1/3)n^(2/3). A separate exact replay generated vertices from all objective orders at n=2..8 and checked the radius and contact counts; a scan through n=1000 found no ties, so the tie rule is justified analytically, not by observed ties.
